synthesis: The coefficient field is structural rather than cosmetic: a finite-field endomorphism algebra can obstruct rational, real, and characteristic-matched p-adic coefficients, while étale, algebraic de Rham, and crystalline constructions supply realizations adapted to different coefficient and characteristic regimes.
source_support: A supersingular elliptic curve has a quaternion endomorphism algebra nonsplit at p and at the real place, excluding Weil cohomology over Q_p, R, and hence Q, while leaving Q_ℓ for ℓ≠p and Witt-fraction coefficients open. Étale torsion groups completed and tensored with Q_ℓ give a Weil theory for ℓ≠p; algebraic de Rham hypercohomology gives one in characteristic zero through comparison; divided-power thickenings lead to crystalline cohomology and, after tensoring Witt vectors with their fraction field, a p-adic Weil theory in characteristic p.
nonparaphrase_operation: The splitting test translates geometric endomorphisms into a module-theoretic compatibility condition, and the three constructions respond with different representation technologies—inverse limits on the étale site, differential hypercohomology, and divided-power infinitesimal thickenings—rather than duplicating one coefficient-neutral object.
limits: The quaternion example excludes only the named coefficient fields and is not a classification. quality_reason: The obstruction unit and construction units jointly explain why multiple realizations are mathematically motivated and how each occupies a different coefficient-sensitive niche, with no claim of universal comparison or exhaustive classification.

Hodge type makes the signed primitive intersection form positive; together these inputs construct an algebraic star and Weil form, and Proposition 3.10 applied to the adjoint relation gives eigenvalue modulus q^(r/2).

synthesis: Deligne's route replaces unavailable algebraic-cycle positivity with an analytic and monodromy-based weight mechanism: even tensor powers make local traces nonnegative, Grothendieck's trace formula turns global cohomology into pole control, big geometric monodromy identifies the relevant invariants, and unbounded powers erase the residual exponent error.
source_support: Landau's theorem lets singularity locations bound Euler roots when coefficients are nonnegative. For a family of odd-dimensional hypersurfaces, traces on E^(⊗2m) are even powers and hence nonnegative; the trace formula expresses the Euler product through compactly supported cohomology, while dense symplectic monodromy identifies coinvariants with Tate-twisted copies whose Frobenius eigenvalue locates the poles. Taking 2m-th roots and duality gives exact local modulus. The main lemma abstracts these inputs, Cartesian powers transfer coarse middle-degree bounds to exact weights, and Lefschetz pencils plus Leray, vanishing cycles, induction, and the cited monodromy theorem complete the general argument.
nonparaphrase_operation: Two amplifiers cooperate: tensor powers convert traces into positive analytic data and divide a fixed pole error by an arbitrarily large power, while Cartesian powers convert a coarse middle-degree window into exact weights and then Künneth and duality transfer the result across degrees. A one-parameter pencil supplies the monodromy representation on which the analytic argument operates.
limits: The route avoids proving the standard conjectures but depends on strong replacement inputs: rational local characteristic polynomials, invariant pairings, sufficiently large monodromy, trace formulas, Lefschetz pencils, vanishing cycles, Leray, and duality.
